transcript.text: Hi, the light in my Neff oven has stopped working (model B1ACE4HN0B). Oven works fine otherwise. Can I change the bulb myself and what bulb do I need?

Yes, you can absolutely change the bulb yourself. It is a simple DIY task that does not require any special tools or technical knowledge.

### 1. The Correct Bulb
For your Neff B1ACE4HN0B oven (which is part of the B1 series), you need:

• Type: Oven lamp bulb, heat-resistant glass
• Wattage: 25 watts (maximum)
• Voltage: 220–240 V
• Base/Socket: E14 (small screw cap)
• Shape: Usually cylindrical or slightly pear-shaped with a clear glass cover.

🔍 Look for bulbs labeled as "Oven Lamp" or "Appliance Bulb" – these are specifically designed to withstand high temperatures inside the oven cavity. Standard household light bulbs will shatter under oven heat.

✅ Recommended search terms:
`Neff oven bulb E14 25W`
or
`25W E14 oven lamp heat resistant`

Brands like Osram, Philips, or GEC make compatible replacements. You can also buy the exact OEM part from Neff spare parts suppliers (part number is often 00438976 or similar – always double-check with your model).

---

### 2. How to Replace the Bulb Safely

#### ⚠️ Safety First:
• Turn off the oven and let it cool completely if it was recently used.
• Switch off the power at the circuit breaker/fuse box for extra safety (optional but recommended).
• Never use a standard light bulb – only use a heat-rated appliance bulb.

#### Steps:
1. Access the bulb: Open the oven door. The bulb is usually located on the top interior ceiling of the oven cavity, behind a glass cover or in a recessed socket.
2. Remove the glass cover (if present): Some models have a small clear plastic/glass shield over the bulb. This may unscrew by hand or be clipped in place. Gently remove it.
3. Unscrew the old bulb: Turn the bulb counter-clockwise gently until it comes free. If it’s tight, use a dry cloth for grip – don’t force it.
4. Insert the new bulb: Screw the new 25W E14 oven bulb in clockwise. Do not overtighten – snug is enough.
5. Replace the cover: Put back any glass shield or cover.
6. Restore power: Turn the breaker back on and test the light by switching the oven on briefly (even if just to check the light).

---

### 3. If the Light Still Doesn’t Work After Replacing the Bulb:
• Ensure the bulb is seated properly.
• Check that the socket isn’t corroded or damaged.
• The issue could be with the oven’s internal wiring, switch, or control board – in which case, contact a qualified technician.
